s0003.literal: Emperor Wen the Shizu, taboo name Qian, style Zihua, was the eldest son of Prince Zhao-lie of Shixing.
s0003.idiomatic: Emperor Wen the Shizu, whose personal name was tabooed as Qian and who styled himself Zihua, was the eldest son of Prince Zhao-lie of Shixing.

s0004.literal: In youth he was deep, keen, and possessed of discernment; handsome in bearing; devoted to the classics and histories; his conduct square and elegant; in every action he unfailingly observed ritual law.
s0004.idiomatic: From youth he was thoughtful, sharp, and far-seeing, with a handsome presence. He steeped himself in the classics and histories, moved with measured grace, and never acted without regard for ritual.

s0005.literal: The Founder loved him greatly and often said, "This boy is the outstanding talent of our clan."
s0005.idiomatic: The Founder adored him and would say, "This son is the finest of our house."

s0006.literal: Early in the Taichu era of Liang he dreamed that two suns fought, one large and one small; the larger sun's light went out and fell to earth, yellow in color, as large as the Dipper; Emperor Wen therefore took one third of it and held it in his bosom.
s0006.idiomatic: Early in Liang's Taichu era he dreamed of two suns at war, one great and one small. The greater sun's light died and fell to earth, yellow and as wide as the Big Dipper; Emperor Wen took a third of it into his breast.

s0007.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion many of his townspeople relied on mountain-and-lake bandits for pillaging; Emperor Wen alone protected his household, and it was never violated.
s0007.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion many neighbors turned to mountain and lake brigands for plunder, but Emperor Wen alone kept his household safe and untouched.

s0008.literal: As disorder grew daily, he fled to Lin'an.
s0008.idiomatic: As chaos deepened day by day, he took refuge at Lin'an.

s0009.literal: When the Founder raised the righteous army, Hou Jing sent messengers to seize Emperor Wen and the Prince Xian of Hengyang; Emperor Wen secretly hid a small knife in his sleeve, hoping to kill Jing when he entered audience; when he arrived he was handed to the officials, and so the plan failed.
s0009.idiomatic: When the Founder raised the righteous army, Hou Jing sent men to seize Emperor Wen and the Prince Xian of Hengyang. Emperor Wen hid a small knife in his sleeve, intending to kill Jing at audience; but on arrival he was turned over to the clerks, and the plot came to nothing.

s0010.literal: The Founder's great army besieged Stone Fortress; Jing several times wished to harm him; when Jing was defeated, Emperor Wen was able to come out and join the Founder's camp.
s0010.idiomatic: The Founder's main force besieged Stone Fortress. Hou Jing more than once meant to kill him; when Jing fell, Emperor Wen at last escaped to the Founder's camp.

s0011.literal: He began his career as Administrator of Wuxing.
s0011.idiomatic: He entered service as administrator of Wuxing.

s0012.literal: At the time the bandit chiefs Ji Ji and Hao Zhong and others each gathered over a thousand men and ravaged the commandery borders; Emperor Wen subdued them.
s0012.idiomatic: Bandit leaders Ji Ji, Hao Zhong, and others had each raised more than a thousand men and were ravaging the commandery; Emperor Wen defeated and pacified them.

s0013.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was appointed Trustworthy Martial General and overseer of South Xuzhou.
s0013.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng (552) he was made Trustworthy Martial General and put in charge of South Xuzhou.

s0014.literal: In the third year the Founder campaigned north to Guangling and made Emperor Wen vanguard; in every battle he was victorious.
s0014.idiomatic: In the third year the Founder marched north against Guangling with Emperor Wen as vanguard; battle after battle went his way.

s0015.literal: When the Founder was about to attack Wang Sengbian, he first summoned Emperor Wen to deliberate.
s0015.idiomatic: Before moving against Wang Sengbian, the Founder called Emperor Wen in to counsel with him.

s0016.literal: Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan held Wuxing with very strong forces; the Founder secretly ordered Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to build palisades against Kan.
s0016.idiomatic: Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan held Wuxing with a formidable host; the Founder secretly ordered Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to throw up palisades against him.

s0017.literal: Emperor Wen had gathered only a few hundred troops and had little military gear; Kan sent his general Du Tai with five thousand elite troops, taking advantage to arrive suddenly; the officers stared at one another pale, but Emperor Wen spoke and laughed as usual, his dispositions clearer still, and so hearts were settled.
s0017.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had barely a few hundred men and scant stores of arms. Kan sent his general Du Tai with five thousand picked troops to strike while the camp was weak. The officers turned pale, but Emperor Wen jested as before, gave his orders with greater clarity, and steadied them.

s0018.literal: Tai knew few were inside the palisade and attacked bitterly day and night; Emperor Wen roused the troops, took arrows and stones upon himself, held for several tens of days, and Tai then retreated.
s0018.idiomatic: Seeing how few defenders the palisade held, Tai pressed the assault day and night. Emperor Wen heartened his men, stood in the line of missile fire himself, and held for many weeks until Tai withdrew.

s0019.literal: When the Founder sent Zhou Wenyü with troops against Kan, Emperor Wen joined the army and went to Wuxing.
s0019.idiomatic: When the Founder dispatched Zhou Wenyü against Du Kan, Emperor Wen marched with him to Wuxing.

s0020.literal: Kan's troops were still numerous, blocking the strategic passes; water and land columns were linked in formation; Emperor Wen ordered the generals Liu Cheng and Jiang Yuanju to lead the attack; Kan's army was greatly defeated, in dire straits, and sued for surrender.
s0020.idiomatic: Kan still fielded a large force, holding the crossings; his fleets and columns were chained together. Emperor Wen sent Liu Cheng and Jiang Yuanju against him. Kan's army was shattered, driven to extremity, and begged to surrender.

s0021.literal: East Yangzhou Inspector Zhang Biao raised troops and besieged Linhai Administrator Wang Huai-zhen; Huai-zhen sent messengers begging rescue; Emperor Wen and Zhou Wenyü led light troops to Kuaiji to strike Biao.
s0021.idiomatic: Zhang Biao, inspector of East Yangzhou, rebelled and besieged Wang Huai-zhen, administrator of Linhai. Huai-zhen sent for help; Emperor Wen and Zhou Wenyü took light forces to Kuaiji to fall upon Biao.

s0022.literal: Later Biao's general Shen Tai opened the gate and admitted Emperor Wen; Emperor Wen took in all his following and their families; when Biao arrived he was again defeated and driven off; the villagers of Ruoye cut off Biao's head and sent it.
s0022.idiomatic: Biao's officer Shen Tai then opened the gates to Emperor Wen, who seized his troops and dependants. When Biao came up he was beaten again and fled. The people of Ruoye slew him and sent his head.

s0023.literal: For his merit he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs over the Ten Commanderies of Kuaiji and Others, General Who Inspires Awe, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
s0023.idiomatic: For these deeds he received the staff of command, authority over military affairs in ten commanderies including Kuaiji, the title General Who Inspires Awe, and the post of administrator of Kuaiji.

s0024.literal: Editorial footnote marker 1. The mountains grew ever deeper and more perilous, and none submitted; Emperor Wen divided his orders and attacked; all were pacified, and his authority and kindness greatly flourished.
s0024.idiomatic: See editorial note 1. In the deep hills many still refused allegiance; Emperor Wen sent columns against them and brought all to order, until his authority and mercy were felt throughout the region.

s0025.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Emperor Wen was enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan with a fief of two thousand households and appointed Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the East.
s0025.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Emperor Wen was made Prince of Linchuan with a fief of two thousand households, palace attendant, and General Who Pacifies the East.

s0026.literal: When Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were defeated at Zhunkou, the Founder ordered Emperor Wen to enter the capital as guard; military stores and war preparations were all entrusted to him.
s0026.idiomatic: After Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were beaten at Zhunkou, the Founder summoned Emperor Wen to defend the capital and placed all grain, arms, and war stores in his hands.

s0027.literal: Soon he was ordered to lead troops south to Wan.
s0027.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to take an army south to Wan.

s0028.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Yongding, on the day wuwu of the cycle, the Founder died; the testamentary edict summoned Emperor Wen to succeed.
s0028.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Yongding (559), on wuwu day, the Founder died; his final edict called Emperor Wen to the succession.

s0029.literal: On the day jiayin he arrived from South Wan and entered the Directorate of the Imperial Secretariat.
s0029.idiomatic: On jiayin day he returned from South Wan and took seat in the Directorate of the Imperial Secretariat.

s0030.literal: The Empress's order said: "High Heaven shows no pity; the Supreme Lord has sent down calamity.
s0030.idiomatic: The empress issued an order: "Heaven shows no pity; the Supreme Lord has sent down calamity.

s0031.literal: The late emperor has suddenly left the myriad states; all within the four seas wail; the whole realm is as in mourning; bitter grief and affliction admit of no escape.
s0031.idiomatic: The late emperor has suddenly left the realm; all under heaven wails as though the sky had fallen; grief beyond bearing has no end.

s0032.literal: The several orphans are slight; there is no date for returning to the state; a chief lord must be established to settle the realm.
s0032.idiomatic: The young princes are helpless and the realm has no master; a ruler must be set up to bring peace to the land.

s0033.literal: Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Prince of Linchuan Qian—his person derives from the Founding Emperor; among the late emperor's sons he is the chosen heir; he raised extraordinary merit at Muye and spread great achievement in pacifying the people; at the time of receiving the chart at Lu, on the day of bearing the throne, he alike assisted the age's harmony and shared in the founding; the ancestral tablets and the far and near all rest their hearts on him. He should receive the great lineage and succeed to the precious record, that the seven temples may have sacrifice and the hundred millions find peace.
s0033.idiomatic: Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Linchuan Qian—born of the imperial line, chosen among the late emperor's sons—won signal merit in the founding wars and spread his fame in pacifying the realm. At the receiving of the mandate and the taking of the throne he shared alike in creation of the dynasty. The altars of state and men far and near look to him. Let him receive the great succession and mount the throne, that the seven temples may be served and the people find rest.

s0034.literal: The one not yet dead borrows lingering breath, bears these hundred afflictions, follows the tangled thread of grief, and speaks with feeling to the breaking point.
s0034.idiomatic: I who am left borrow a little breath more, bear a hundred griefs, trace this tangled sorrow, and cannot speak without breaking.

s0035.literal: " Emperor Wen firmly declined, even to a third time; the dukes, ministers, and scholars firmly pressed him; that very day he ascended the imperial throne in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
s0035.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen refused firmly, again and again; the nobles and officials pressed him without relent; that same day he took the throne in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

s0036.literal: An edict said: "Heaven has sent down calamity and gathered upon the state; the late emperor has left the myriad states; all within the soil have hearts that break; it is as though one had lost father and mother.
s0036.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Heaven has sent calamity upon the realm; the late emperor has left us; all the land is stricken as by the death of a parent.

s0037.literal: The dragon chart and precious calendar are faintly placed upon Our person; the age's fortune meets disturbance; affairs press upon the pivot of power; the south must have a lord; western yielding makes ritual light; We now formally receive the bright mandate and brightly dwell in the four seas.
s0037.idiomatic: The dragon chart and sacred calendar have fallen to Our person; the times are turbulent and the helm cannot wait; the realm needs a ruler, and modest refusal would slight the rites. We now take the bright mandate and rule the four seas.

s0038.literal: A great amnesty is proclaimed for all under heaven; crimes whether light or heavy are all washed away.
s0038.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm; crimes light or heavy are all pardoned.

s0039.literal: Overdue rents and old debts, and offenses and debts of officials and people, shall not again be collected.
s0039.idiomatic: Arrears of tax and old debts, and penalties owed by officials and commoners, shall not be collected again.

s0040.literal: Civil and military, within and without, shall receive promotions of rank in due measure.
s0040.idiomatic: Civil and military officers at court and in the provinces shall be advanced in rank as their service warrants.

s0041.literal: Those filial, dutiful, and diligent in farming who are heirs to their fathers shall be granted one rank of nobility.
s0041.idiomatic: Men noted for filial piety and farming, who are heirs to their fathers, shall receive one step in noble rank.

s0042.literal: Let awe and respect dwell in every heart and the ministers give their full strength; to overcome cruelty and remove killing need not wait a hundred years.
s0042.idiomatic: Let reverence fill every heart and the ministers give their all; to end cruelty and slaughter need not wait a century.

s0043.literal: Speaking brings choked sobs and deep increase of grief to the breaking point.
s0043.idiomatic: Even to speak of it chokes Us with grief beyond bearing.

s0044.literal: " Another edict ordered all provinces and commanderies to halt envoys rushing to court.
s0044.idiomatic: " A further edict ordered every province and commandery to stop dispatching envoys in haste to the capital.

s0045.literal: In the seventh month, autumn, on the day chen of the cycle, the empress was honored as Empress Dowager.
s0045.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on chen day, the empress was honored as empress dowager.

s0046.literal: On the day jiwei, Pacifying South General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Guangzhou Ouyang Yi was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns South; Pacifying South General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Zhou Di was advanced in title to General Who Guards the South; Editorial footnote marker 2. Pacifying South General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Gaozhou Huang Faqu was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South.
s0046.idiomatic: On jiwei day Ouyang Yi, pacifying south general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Guangzhou, was promoted to general who campaigns south; Zhou Di, pacifying south general and grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, was promoted to general who guards the south; See editorial note 2. Huang Faqu, pacifying south general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Gaozhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the south.

s0047.literal: On the day gengshen, Guarding South Grand General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Guizhou Chunyu Liang was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns South.
s0047.idiomatic: On gengshen day Chunyu Liang, guarding south grand general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Guizhou, was promoted to general who campaigns south.

s0048.literal: On the day xinyou, Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Minister of Works Hou Tian became Grand Mentor; Pacifying West General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of South Yuzhou Hou Andu became Minister of Works; Palace Attendant, Central Authority General, and Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Wang Chong became Special Grand Master and Left Grand Master of the Palace; Guarding North General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou Xu Du became Palace Attendant, Central Pacifying General, and Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
s0048.idiomatic: On xinyou day Hou Tian, palace attendant, general of chariots and cavalry, and minister of works, became grand mentor; Hou Andu, pacifying west general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and inspector of South Yuzhou, became minister of works; Wang Chong, palace attendant, central authority general, and grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, became special grand master and left grand master of the palace; Xu Du, guarding north general and inspector of South Xuzhou, became palace attendant, central pacifying general, and grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes.

s0049.literal: On the day renxu, Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army Xu Shipu became Special Grand Master and General Who Pacifies the Right;
s0049.idiomatic: On renxu day Xu Shipu, palace attendant and general who protects the army, was made special grand master and general who pacifies the right;

s0050.literal: Palace Attendant and Loyal Martial General Du Ling became General of the Palace Guards.
s0050.idiomatic: Du Ling, palace attendant and loyal martial general, was made general of the palace guards.

s0051.literal: On the day yichou the Hall of Layered Clouds caught fire.
s0051.idiomatic: On yichou day the Hall of Layered Clouds burned.

s0052.literal: In the eighth month, on the day guisi, Pacifying North General and Inspector of South Xuzhou Liu Yi became General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jinyang; Pacifying South General and Inspector of North Jiangzhou Lu Sida was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the Left.
s0052.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guisi day, Liu Yi, pacifying north general and inspector of South Xuzhou, became general who pacifies the south and inspector of Jinyang; Lu Sida, pacifying south general and inspector of North Jiangzhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the left.

s0053.literal: On the day gengxu the prince Bomao was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing, Editorial footnote marker 3. to continue the line of Prince Zhao-lie.
s0053.idiomatic: On gengxu day the prince Bomao was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing, See editorial note 3. as heir to Prince Zhao-lie.

s0054.literal: The heir of Shixing, Prince Xu, was transferred in enfeoffment to Prince of Ancheng.
s0054.idiomatic: Xu, heir of Shixing, was transferred to the title Prince of Ancheng.

s0056.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinyou, the prince Bozong was established as crown prince; Editorial footnote marker 5. dukes, marquises, and those below were granted silk cloth in differing amounts.
s0056.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinyou day, the prince Bozong was made crown prince; See editorial note 5. princes, nobles, and officials received gifts of silk in varying measure.

s0057.literal: On the day yihai the consort of the surname Shen was established as empress.
s0057.idiomatic: On yihai day Lady Shen was made empress.

s0058.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on the day yimao, Wang Lin raided Dalei; an edict dispatched Grand Mentor Hou Tian, Minister of Works Hou Andu, and Commissioner with Equal Protocol Xu Du to lead troops against him.
s0058.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao day, Wang Lin attacked Dalei. An edict sent Hou Tian, grand mentor, Hou Andu, minister of works, and Xu Du, commissioner with equal protocol, with armies to meet him.

s0059.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Tianjia, on the day guichou, an edict said: "We, slight and dim, have succeeded to the great enterprise; the orphaned and alone are in affliction; the way of rule is not yet clear; looking up to former virtue, the hidden and manifest are far extended; reverently holding Ourselves in check and not speaking, We hope there may be no change.
s0059.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Tianjia (560), on guichou day, an edict declared: "We, unworthy and obscure, have inherited the great enterprise. The realm is orphaned and We are in mourning; government is not yet settled. Looking to the virtue of those before Us, We would reach both the seen and unseen; holding Ourself in reverent silence, We hope for steady rule.

s0060.literal: Though the great plan and splendid track, sun and moon are just now broadening, yet the clear temple stands empty and the sage spirit grows ever distant; moved to follow what is forever gone, gazing in speech We find no limit.
s0060.idiomatic: Though Our great design spreads wide as sun and moon, the ancestral temple stands empty and the sage spirit recedes. Following thought to what is gone forever, We look up and find no end to grief.

s0061.literal: Now the four images turn through the cycle, the three origins announce their offering; Chinese and barbarian alike reach the shore; jade and silk gallop in; We think to extend the lingering grace and spread it to the hundred millions.
s0061.idiomatic: Now the seasons turn their round and heaven's gifts are renewed; far peoples and near come to court; tribute pours in. We mean to spread the late emperor's bounty to the hundred millions.

s0062.literal: A great amnesty is proclaimed for all under heaven.
s0062.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm.

s0063.literal: The fourth year of Yongding is changed to the first year of Tianjia.
s0063.idiomatic: The fourth year of Yongding is renamed the first year of Tianjia.

s0064.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves shall be given five hu of grain per person.
s0064.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute who cannot support themselves shall receive five hu of grain each.

s0065.literal: Those filial, dutiful, and diligent in farming of exceptional conduct and special merit shall receive one additional rank of nobility.
s0065.idiomatic: Men outstanding in filial piety, farming, or singular virtue shall receive one further step in noble rank.

s0066.literal: On the day jiayin envoys were separately dispatched to proclaim comfort to the four quarters.
s0066.idiomatic: On jiayin day envoys were sent out to announce Our goodwill to the four quarters.

s0067.literal: On the day xinyou the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb; an edict said: "We perform the offering to the Supreme Lord above, reverently present the victim and jade; when the great suburban rite is complete, sincerity and respect are alike broadened.
s0067.idiomatic: On xinyou day the emperor sacrificed in person at the Southern Suburb. An edict said: "We have offered to the Supreme Lord above and reverently presented victims and jade; the great suburban rite is complete, and devotion fills Our heart.

s0068.literal: Moreover, yin gloom had drenched the days, yet the canopy cleared on this day; clouds and things were bright and clear, wind and scenery pure and harmonious; rejoicing moved human spirits and gladness flowed among the people; Editorial footnote marker 6. We think to make the black-haired people share this abundant blessing.
s0068.idiomatic: Though gloom had hung for many days, the sky cleared today; clouds shone fair and the air was mild; joy touched heaven and earth and gladness ran among the people. See editorial note 6. We would have the common folk share this blessing.

s0069.literal: The people may be granted one rank of nobility.
s0069.idiomatic: Let the people receive one step in noble rank.

s0070.literal: " On the day xinwei the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.
s0070.idiomatic: " On xinwei day the emperor sacrificed in person at the Northern Suburb.

s0072.literal: In the second month, on the day xinmao, the Old Man star appeared.
s0072.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao day, the Old Man star was seen.

s0073.literal: On the day yiwei, Inspector of Gaozhou Ji Ji rebelled from the army and returned to Xuancheng, holding the commandery in response to Wang Lin; Jing Magistrate He Dangqian campaigned and pacified him.
s0073.idiomatic: On yiwei day Ji Ji, inspector of Gaozhou, deserted his command, returned to Xuancheng, and held the commandery for Wang Lin. He Dangqian, magistrate of Jing, marched against him and restored order.

s0074.literal: On the day shen of the cycle, Grand Mentor Hou Tian defeated Wang Lin at Liangshan and defeated Qi troops at Bowang; he captured alive the Qi general Liu Boqiu, took all their stores and ships, captives and severed ears numbered in the tens of thousands; Wang Lin and his lord Xiao Zhuang fled to Qi.
s0074.idiomatic: On shen day Grand Mentor Hou Tian routed Wang Lin at Liangshan and crushed Northern Qi forces at Bowang. He took the Qi general Liu Boqiu alive, seized their stores and fleet, and counted captives and heads by the ten thousand. Wang Lin and his puppet ruler Xiao Zhuang fled to Qi.

s0075.literal: On the day wuxu an edict said: "The five fortunes come in turn, the three numina bestow mandate; emperors and kings thereby change and create; Yin and Zhou therefore took joy in pushing him forward.
s0075.idiomatic: On wuxu day an edict declared: "The five fortunes succeed one another and the three spirits grant the mandate; thus emperors and kings renew the realm, as Yin and Zhou once gladly raised their chosen men.

s0076.literal: We have inherited the calendar and received the foundation, greatly elevated the tripod's fortune; the term of rule is where it belongs, the span of blessing is here; how could it be reached by chance? Surely the tortoise and prayer could not obtain it.
s0076.idiomatic: We have taken the calendar and received the foundation, exalted the dynasty's fortune; the age of rule is Ours by right, the blessing of years rests here—not by chance, nor by divination alone.

s0077.literal: Thus one knows the weight of the sacred vessel must lie in the talisman and mandate.
s0077.idiomatic: So one knows the throne's weight lies in heaven's sign and mandate.

s0078.literal: Therefore chasing the deer brought reproach, cutting the snake fixed the enterprise; rebellious ministers and wicked sons share the same fault across ages.
s0078.idiomatic: Thus the chase for the deer drew blame, while the cut serpent secured the realm; traitors and rebels wear the same guilt in every age.

s0079.literal: Wang Lin's knowledge was dim in holding the bottle, his wisdom ashamed before guarding the foot; he violated the norm and disturbed order, bringing downfall on himself; yet many gentlemen of the gentry were bound and held; though the Jing and Wei mingled their waters and orchid and leek lay in the same market, seeking the principle thereof, some may have followed under compulsion.
s0079.idiomatic: Wang Lin knew too little to hold his charge and lacked wit enough to save himself; he broke the laws and brought ruin on his own head. Yet many gentry were taken bound with him; though the guilty and the innocent were heaped together, some surely followed under duress.

s0080.literal: Now the nine nets are set, the eight cords drawn shut; heaven's net is vast and wide, yet the great fish may slip through.
s0080.idiomatic: Now the nets are spread and the eight directions closed in; heaven's net is wide, yet even great offenders may pass through its meshes.

s0081.literal: As for Fubo roaming in persuasion, forever becoming Han's frontier guard; Shou forever escaping and returning, in the end becoming Wei's border warden—the vessel changed with Qin and Yu, talent passed between Jin and Chu; going, staying, using, and discarding—how could they be constant? We should add broad kindness to display thunder's work.
s0081.idiomatic: Ma Yuan once wandered as envoy and became a frontier guard of Han; Cai Yong fled home and ended a warden of Wei—men change with the times, talent flows between states; who stays or goes is not fixed forever. Let Us show the mercy of thunder's season.

s0082.literal: Gentry and clans who beforehand were in the wicked faction are all pardoned;
s0082.idiomatic: Gentry and clans who joined the rebel faction are all forgiven;

s0083.literal: generals and fighting troops are likewise pardoned in the same amnesty; Editorial footnote marker 7. and according to talent they shall be appointed and led forth, that We may gather their use.
s0083.idiomatic: commanders and common soldiers share the same pardon; See editorial note 7. let them be placed by merit, that We may put their strength to use.

s0084.literal: " Another edict: since the armies marched, officers and soldiers who died for the royal affair shall all receive posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous titles.
s0084.idiomatic: " A further edict: all officers and soldiers who died in the royal service since the campaigns began shall receive posthumous honors and titles.

s0085.literal: On the day jihai an edict said: "Recently the wicked chieftain ran riot; the armies advanced in punishment; ships and transports piled up; corvée and labor were borrowed from the people; the armies were out for a long time and service and toil lasted many days.
s0085.idiomatic: On jihai day an edict declared: "Lately the rebel chief ravaged the land; Our armies marched to punish him. Ships and supplies piled high; the people were pressed for labor; the hosts were long in the field and toil ran on for months.

s0086.literal: Now the evil vapors are cleared and the realm made pure; there should be discrimination and relief.
s0086.idiomatic: Now the omens of disorder have cleared; let mercy sort the harmed from the guilty.

s0087.literal: Corvée service and personal levies may be remitted.
s0087.idiomatic: Corvée drafts and personal levies are remitted.

s0088.literal: Husbands and wives of three years' standing, if one died in service by misfortune, their wives and children shall be restored.
s0088.idiomatic: Where husband and wife had been wed three years and one died on campaign, the survivor and children shall be released from obligation.

s0089.literal: On the day gengzi envoys were separately dispatched bearing the imperial seal and writings to proclaim comfort to the four quarters.
s0089.idiomatic: On gengzi day envoys were sent bearing the imperial seal and edicts to announce Our goodwill to the four quarters.

s0090.literal: On the day yisi Grand Mentor Hou Tian was sent to guard Pen City.
s0090.idiomatic: On yisi day Grand Mentor Hou Tian was sent to hold Pen City.

s0091.literal: On the day gengxu the Founder's sixth son Chang was made Rapid Tiger General and Governor of Xiangzhou and established as Prince of Hengyang.
s0091.idiomatic: On gengxu day Chang, the Founder's sixth son, was made Rapid Tiger General and governor of Xiangzhou and enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang.

s0092.literal: In the third month, on the day chen of the cycle, an edict said: "Since disorder and ruin, more than ten years have passed; registered households have withered away, not one in ten thousand remains; the common people of the central plains can scarcely be said to exist.
s0092.idiomatic: In the third month, on chen day, an edict declared: "Since rebellion and ruin more than ten years have passed. Registered households have dwindled until scarcely one in ten thousand remains; the people of the heartland can hardly be said to survive.

s0093.literal: Recently bandit troubles have come in succession and reckonings and levies have been numerous; moreover, since the armies were raised, a thousand gold is spent each day; the treasury is emptied and the loom's shuttle wears thin year by year.
s0093.idiomatic: Lately raids have followed raids and taxes have multiplied; since war began a thousand gold flows out each day. The treasury stands empty and every household is scraped bare.

s0094.literal: The military grain lately set aside was originally to fill war stores; now the chief villain is destroyed and the eight regions are already at peace; arms are stilled and shoulders may rest; We think to make the remaining people receive this broad tax relief; this year's military grain shall be reduced by one third throughout.
s0094.idiomatic: The grain lately levied for the armies was meant for war stores; now the arch-rebel is dead and the realm is calm, weapons are laid by and the people may breathe. We would ease the burden on those who remain: this year's military grain levy is cut by one third.

s0095.literal: The Masters of Writing shall send down to the four quarters, voicing Our compassionate intent.
s0095.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing shall proclaim this mercy to every province.

s0096.literal: Local administrators shall clearly urge farming and mulberry; let bellies be drummed full and mouths nursed in peace—may that day return soon.
s0096.idiomatic: Magistrates must urge plowing and sericulture with all their power, that men may once more drum their full bellies and nurse their children in peace.

s0097.literal: " Sun Yang, whom Xiao Zhuang had appointed Inspector of Yingzhou, led the whole commandery to submit.
s0097.idiomatic: " Sun Yang, whom Xiao Zhuang had named inspector of Yingzhou, brought the entire commandery over to Our side.

s0098.literal: On the day dingsi Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhou Di pacified the southern center, beheaded the bandit leader Xiong Tanlang, and sent his head to the capital.
s0098.idiomatic: On dingsi day Zhou Di, inspector of Jiangzhou, pacified the southern center, slew the rebel chief Xiong Tanlang, and sent his head to the capital.

s0099.literal: Earlier Northern Qi troops had held Lushan city; on the day wuwu the Qi army abandoned the city and fled; an edict ordered Inspector of South Yuzhou Cheng Lingxiu to hold it.
s0099.idiomatic: Northern Qi had held Lushan city; on wuwu day the Qi garrison abandoned it and fled. An edict put Cheng Lingxiu, inspector of South Yuzhou, in charge of the place.

s0100.literal: On the day jiazi the four commanderies of Tianmen, Yiyang, and Nanping from Jingzhou and Wuling from Yingzhou were separated out to establish Wuzhou.
s0100.idiomatic: On jiazi day Tianmen, Yiyang, and Nanping were taken from Jingzhou and Wuling from Yingzhou to form the new province of Wu.
